hints: Use logarithm laws to combine the right-hand side into a single logarithm.
Rewrite $2\ln x$ as $\ln x^2$ and combine the subtraction as a quotient, then equate the positive arguments.
Clear the denominator to obtain a quadratic equation and solve it.
Check both candidates against $2x-3>0$ and $x-1>0$, retaining only the valid solution before rounding to 2 decimal places.
walkthrough:
Start from the given logarithmic equation:
$$\ln(2x - 3) = 2\ln x - \ln(x - 1)$$

Apply the power law of logarithms to rewrite the term $2\ln x$:
$$2\ln x = \ln(x^2)$$
$$\ln(2x - 3) = \ln(x^2) - \ln(x - 1)$$

Apply the quotient law of logarithms $\ln A - \ln B = \ln\left(\dfrac{A}{B}\right)$:
$$\ln(2x - 3) = \ln\left(\dfrac{x^2}{x - 1}\right)$$

Exponentiate both sides to eliminate the natural logarithm:
$$2x - 3 = \dfrac{x^2}{x - 1}$$

Expand the left-hand side:
$$2x^2 - 2x - 3x + 3 = x^2$$
$$2x^2 - 5x + 3 = x^2$$

Subtract $x^2$ from both sides to form a 3-term quadratic equation:
$$x^2 - 5x + 3 = 0$$

Apply the quadratic formula $x = \dfrac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a}$ with $a = 1$, $b = -5$, and $c = 3$:
$$x = \dfrac{-(-5) \pm \sqrt{(-5)^2 - 4(1)(3)}}{2(1)} = \dfrac{5 \pm \sqrt{25 - 12}}{2} = \dfrac{5 \pm \sqrt{13}}{2}$$

Check against the domain restrictions of the original equation:
For the logarithms to be defined, the arguments must be positive:
$$2x - 3 > 0 \implies x > 1.5$$
$$x > 0$$
$$x - 1 > 0 \implies x > 1$$
Hence $x$ must be strictly greater than $1.5$.
Since $x_2 \approx 0.70 < 1.5$, it is invalid and must be discarded.

Round the valid root to 2 decimal places:
$$x \approx 4.30$$
